bodyMarkdown:
## Pharmacist Salary Sydney Under the Pharmacy Industry Award

If you are looking at a **pharmacist salary Sydney** offer or wondering what you should be paid, the starting point is the Pharmacy Industry Award 2020. This award sets the minimum hourly rates for pharmacists, pharmacy assistants, pharmacy students and pharmacy interns. The rates are updated each year by the Fair Work Commission, and the figures below apply from the first full pay period starting on or after 1 July 2026.

### Minimum Hourly Rates for Pharmacists

Under the award, a pharmacist is classified at one of four levels depending on experience and responsibility:

- **Pharmacist** – $41.74 per hour ($1,586.30 per week)
- **Experienced pharmacist** – $45.72 per hour ($1,737.40 per week)
- **Pharmacist in charge** – $46.80 per hour ($1,778.40 per week)
- **Pharmacist manager** – $52.15 per hour ($1,981.60 per week)

These are the minimum rates for full-time and part-time employees. A full-time pharmacist works 38 ordinary hours per week (or 76 hours over two consecutive weeks). A part-time pharmacist works fewer than 38 hours per week on reasonably predictable hours.

### Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay

The standard formula to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time pharmacist on $41.74 per hour working 38 hours each week:

$41.74 × 38 × 52 = $82,481 per year (rounded)

This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances and no salary sacrifice. If you work more than 38 hours, overtime rates apply (150% for the first two hours Monday to Saturday, 200% after that, 200% on Sunday and 250% on public holidays).

For a fortnightly comparison, multiply the weekly rate by two. A pharmacist on $1,586.30 per week earns $3,172.60 per fortnight before tax.

### Casual Loading of 25%

Casual employees under the Pharmacy Industry Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. The casual rates are:

- **Pharmacist (casual)** – $52.18 per hour
- **Experienced pharmacist (casual)** – $57.15 per hour
- **Pharmacist in charge (casual)** – $58.50 per hour
- **Pharmacist manager (casual)** – $65.19 per hour

If you are a casual pharmacist working 38 hours in a week, your gross pay would be $52.18 × 38 = $1,982.84 for that week. The casual loading is paid on ordinary hours only and is not applied to overtime.

For more detail on how casual loading interacts with award rates, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide.

### Super Guarantee Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time pharmacist earning $82,481 per year, the employer contributes an additional $9,898 in super. This is not deducted from your salary – it is paid into your super fund on top.

For casual employees, super is calculated on the casual rate (including the 25% loading) because the casual loading forms part of ordinary time earnings. A casual pharmacist earning $52.18 per hour would have super calculated on that rate.

Learn more about how super fits into your total package on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Tax Estimates for 2026–27

The Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates for 2026–27 are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. For a full-time pharmacist earning $82,481 per year, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be roughly $16,500 to $17,500 depending on your exact circumstances. This is an estimate only – use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a more personalised figure.

### How the Award Compares to the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. The casual rate including 25% loading is $33.05 per hour. A pharmacist rate of $41.74 per hour is well above the minimum, reflecting the professional qualifications and responsibility required.

For a full comparison of award classifications and rates, see our [reference tables](/data) and the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a full-time pharmacist on $41.74 per hour:

- Weekly: $41.74 × 38 = $1,586.12
- Fortnightly: $1,586.12 × 2 = $3,172.24

After tax and Medicare, the fortnightly take-home pay would be approximately $2,600 to $2,700, depending on your tax file number declaration and any other deductions.

### Summary

A **pharmacist salary Sydney** under the Pharmacy Industry Award starts at $41.74 per hour for a full-time pharmacist, rising to $52.15 per hour for a pharmacist manager. Casual employees receive 25% loading, taking the casual pharmacist rate to $52.18 per hour. Super of 12% is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to estimate annual gross pay, and remember that penalty rates, overtime and allowances can increase your actual earnings.

For a quick calculation of your own rate, try [the timesheet](/).
